★★★ `.section NAME` AND THE RESERVE-WITH-FILL FAMILY, READ BACK AT RUNTIME — the x86_64 half. ✔MEASURED 2026-08-13: pe64 exits 42 on Windows (debug AND release), elf64 exits 42 on WSL x86_64 (debug AND release).

★★★ WHY THIS EXAMPLE EXISTS, STATED AS A MEASUREMENT RATHER THAN A RATIONALE. ✔MEASURED before it was written: `grep -rn '^\s*\.\(section\|space\|zero\|skip\)' examples/asm/*/main.s` returned NOTHING. `AsmDirectiveVerb::SectionByName` and `AsmDirectiveVerb::ReserveFillBytes` shipped declared in BOTH dialect documents and handled in `asm_text_to_lir.cpp`, and every claim about them rested on unit tests over an in-memory `dataItems` vector. A unit test cannot see whether those bytes reach the IMAGE, at the right OFFSETS, with the right CONTENTS — this repo has the scar: a lowering computed `dataItems` and the driver dropped them on the floor; the mutant compiled clean, produced an artifact, and only an image-level witness caught it.

★★ EVERY BYTE RESERVED IS LOADED AGAIN BY THE PROGRAM THAT RESERVED IT, and the answer is a SUM of what was read (20 + 7 + 15 + 0 = 42), not a constant. Each quadword is ALSO compared against what it must be and lands on its own numbered arm (11/12/13/14) when it is not — so a wrong byte cannot collide with 42 by arithmetic accident, and the failing arm says WHICH quadword was wrong.

★★★ THE DISCRIMINATION IS MEASURED, ARM BY ARM. ✔MEASURED 2026-08-13 by rebuilding this same file with ONE directive operand changed (each mutant checked byte-wise against the base before it was compiled, so an arm that failed to land is reported VOID rather than counted):
  • `.space 1, 20` -> `.space 1, 21`   exit 11  (the fill BYTE)
  • `.space 1, 20` -> `.space 1`       exit 11  (the fill DROPPED — what the verb did before it was modelled)
  • `.skip 7`      -> `.skip 6`        exit 11  (the reserve's SIZE)
  • `.quad 7`      -> `.quad 9`        exit 12  (the emitData that follows the reserves)
  • `.zero 1, 15`  -> `.zero 1, 0`     exit 13  (`.zero` carries a fill too)
  • `.space 7`     -> `.space 7, 1`    exit 13  (a fill appearing where none was named)
  • `.section .bss` -> `.section .data` exit 14 (the SECTION the operand names)
  • `.section .rodata` -> `.rodata`     REFUSED, A0008, 'is a SECTION NAME in this dialect, not a directive'
  • `.section .rodata` -> `.section .rodata,@progbits`  REFUSED, A0008, 'carries 2 operands; this build models the section NAME and nothing else'
  ⓘ AND ONE CONTROL THAT MUST **NOT** MOVE: `.space 8, 3` -> `.space 8, 0` in `.bss` stays exit 42, because a zero-fill section stores no file bytes and BOTH fills are correctly ignored. An arm that changed here would mean the fill was reaching the wire, which is the defect in the other direction.

★★ THE `.bss` FILL IS WHAT MAKES THE SECTION'S IDENTITY RUNTIME-OBSERVABLE, and it is the reason that line names a fill it does not want. `.space 8, 3` in a zero-fill section is warned-and-ignored (gas does exactly this: `Warning: ignoring fill value in section '.bss'`, exit 0). Route that section to a file-backed one by mistake and the SAME directive writes eight 0x03 bytes — which is the `.section .bss` -> `.section .data` arm above, exit 14. Without the fill, that mutant would still exit 42 and the section's identity would have no runtime witness at all.
  ⓘ THE WARNING IS TOLERATED BY DESIGN, NOT BY LUCK: ✔MEASURED in `tests/examples/examples_runner.cpp`, the compile-side gate is `EXPECT_EQ(rep.errorCount(), 0u)` — ERROR severity only. A future change that promoted warnings would red this example, which is the correct thing for it to do.

★★ WHAT THIS FIXTURE DOES **NOT** SEPARATE, said plainly rather than left to be discovered: `.rodata` versus `.data` is NOT distinguishable from inside the process without attempting a write, so a mutant routing `.section .rodata` to the `.data` row still exits 42. That property is pinned where it can be seen — `tests/asm/test_asm_text_to_lir.cpp` asserts `.section .rodata` reaches `DataSectionKind::Rodata` and `.section .data` reaches `Data`. The corpus adds what the unit tier cannot: that the bytes survive the section assignment, the linker's layout and the loader's mapping, on two object formats.

★★ THE DELEGATION IS THE POINT OF `sectionByName` AND IT IS EXERCISED THREE WAYS HERE. `.section` mints no second section vocabulary — it resolves its operand against this dialect's OWN section-opening rows, so `.section .data` and a bare `.data` reach the identical row by construction. This file drives all three: `.rodata` (reachable ONLY as an operand — the row is `operandOnly` and the bare spelling is refused), `.data` (reachable both ways), and `.bss`.

⚠ NO arm64 LEG HERE, DELIBERATELY: this file is x86_64 AT&T assembly and names x86 registers, so it is not portable text. Its sibling `asm_arm64_section_reserve_fill_readback` carries BYTE-IDENTICAL directive text with this CPU's instructions swapped for AArch64's, and ✔MEASURED the SAME nine exit codes under qemu-aarch64 — which is the actual claim, since the directives are one engine's verbs and only the dialect spellings differ.

★ THE `release` ARM, SCOPED HONESTLY. At the `encode` tier no MIR module exists, so the optimizer, the register allocator and calling-convention materialization never run — this arm does NOT witness the optimizer and cannot. It pins the narrower fact that `--config=release` still produces a working binary from assembly, and it is ✔MEASURED at 42 rather than assumed.
